EV061, EV013, GX009, and EV031 are transferred only as source observations that amines and solvent environments can alter CO2 association, proton availability, viscosity, conductivity, coordination environment, and intermediate stability. The proposal therefore compares TEA and TEOA within one anchored formulation family, adds no-amine and Ar controls for attribution, and narrows inference because composition normalization cannot make the anchored recipe becomes substantially smaller or disappears in the normalized comparison, while the CO2 and no-amine controls show that the normalized experiment still produces attributable signal. This would indicate that recipe-linked medium effects contribute materially, without identifying which hidden variable is responsible.","refutes":"Refutes the stronger medium-dominant emphasis of H03 if the TEA/TEOA difference is reproduced with similar direction and magnitude in both anchored and normalized comparisons, suggesting that the controlled composition variables are not the main source of the selectivity difference. That outcome would be more compatible with donor-specific redox, coordination, or cobalt-state alternatives, though not uniquely proving any one of them.","inconclusive":"Inconclusive if one or more normalized groups give signal near detection limits, if normalization causes incompatible catalyst stability or phase behavior, if the Ar or no-amine controls reveal strong background artifacts, or if the observed TEA/TEOA differences are comparable to run-to-run analytical uncertainty.","parameter_selection":"Do not invent literature values. Use the EV059-linked recipe family only to choose the starting composition logic, then pilot the minimum necessary executable settings: catalyst loading window, support amount, irradiation time, sampling interval, and gas calibration range. For normalized groups, hold MeCN/H2O ratio and total amine-derived fraction constant across TEA and TEOA where physically feasible; if miscibility or handling prevents exact matching, document the deviation and narrow the inference rather than asserting equivalence.","limitations":"TEA and TEOA remain chemically nonequivalent even after composition normalization, so this card cannot isolate proton activity, dissolved CO2, viscosity, conductivity, and cobalt coordination effects from one another. The no-amine comparison also changes overall liquid composition and therefore tests functional necessity more than pure mechanistic causality. Product data alone cannot identify the active cobalt species or the dominant hidden variable behind any selectivity shift.","feasibility":"low_cost"}]}
